top news.title: OpenAI says its models, including GPT-5.6 Sol and “an even more capable pre-release model”, breached Hugging Face while OpenAI tested their cyber capabilities

tweets.author: @ryangreenblatt
tweets.text: It's good that OpenAI reported this.  It's concerning (though perhaps predictable) that it happened.  Reward hacking can go very far.  I think generalizing all the way to a full AI takeover is possible for extremely capable AIs.  And “smaller” incidents like temporarily launching rogue deployments or seizing control of some compute are plausible earlier.  I think we'll see increasingly large incidents like this one over time

tweets.author: @deanwball
tweets.text: A couple years ago, the AI debate was centered, rightfully, on whether crazy-sounding things like “AIs autonomously making math breakthroughs” and “AIs breaking from their sandbox and hacking on the internet” would be real things in the near term.  Sometimes it feels like that's still the debate we're having.  This can be frustrating, because in my view, that debate is settled and was settled quite a while ago.

tweets.author: @troyhunt
tweets.text: Not sure if this is a mea culpa or a “look at how awesome our AI has become”. Maybe both? 🤷‍♂️

sub_items.title: OpenAI says its models chained vulnerabilities across its research environment and Hugging Face's infrastructure to find solutions for the ExploitGym benchmark

top news.title: Google launches Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber, and says it has started its “most ambitious pre-training run yet” for Gemini 4

tweets.author: @joshwoodward
tweets.text: Today's launches are all about better performance, lower latency, and a smaller bill.  + 3.6 Flash cuts token usage by up to 65% on complex coding + 3.5 Flash-Lite reaches speeds of 350 output tokens/sec Both are live in the Gemini app today!  Next up: Gemini 3.5 Pro, which has officially entered partner testing.

tweets.author: @kimmonismus
tweets.text: Google has begun pre-training Gemini 4, marking a completely new foundation model.  This is really exciting!  The announcement blog for 3.6 Flash states that Gemini 4 is being completely revamped.  Presumably, the recent developments for 3.5 Pro were disappointing, so they're starting with a new pre-training program.  This could be interesting!

tweets.author: @shakeelhashim
tweets.text: Note the timing here — Alphabet reports earnings tomorrow, and is sure to face questions from investors asking why GDM appears to have fallen so far behind OpenAI and Anthropic.

sub_items.title: Google prices Gemini 3.6 Flash lower than 3.5 Flash, at $1.50/1M input tokens and $7.50/1M output tokens, and Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite at $0.30/1M and $2.50/1M
Google says Gemini 3.6 Flash improves coding, multimodal, and knowledge work performance and uses up to 17% fewer tokens and costs less per token vs. 3.5 Flash
Google says Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber is a “cost-efficient and highly capable alternative” to models like Mythos, available first to governments and some partners

top news.title: Sources: China is weighing tightening AI and chip export controls and is consulting leading domestic AI companies, in a bid to slow advanced tech acquisitions

tweets.author: @quxiaoyin
tweets.text: China could ban domestic user traces from being sold to US labs, but they won't ban open-weight models. They are benefiting from it tremendously now.

tweets.author: @himanshustwts
tweets.text: Yesterday: US administration is reportedly considering restrictions on advanced Chinese AI models such as Kimi K3 and DeepSeek.  Today: China is considering tightening its export controls on AI tech and would restrict non-Chinese nationals from downloading the open weights of frontier Chinese models.  Wild tradeoffs.

tweets.author: @emollick
tweets.text: And now from the Chinese government side. This would be a good time for cooperation between the US and China to establish common testing/acceptance standards for new models, so at least the safety certification side of model releases can be transparent for open & closed models.
